warnings.label: Christchurch Harbour
warnings.message:
There is no longer a threat of flooding, though standing water and debris may still remain. 
We do not expect to see similar impacts from the next high tide.  
We will continue to monitor the situation and will issue further alerts or warnings if necessary.  
Continue to take care on waterside roads and footpaths and don't put yourself in unnecessary danger. Never drive through flood water,  just 30cm of fast flowing water is enough to move your car.

warnings.label: Hunstanton coast in Norfolk
warnings.message:
High tides tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 06:00am to 10:00am on Sunday 13 September 2026. 
Areas most at risk are around Hunstanton seafront. Flood gates in the area will be closed by the Local Authority which will make access difficult. The detailed forecast is for a peak level at King's Lynn of 4.67mAODN at 08:15am on 13 September, Wind Force 3, Westerly. The current series of high spring tides has now reached its peak and will fall away over the next few days. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid beaches and coastal promenades, which may be flooded . 
This message will be updated by 11:00AM on 13 September 2026 or as the situation changes.

warnings.label: Somerset coast at Porlock Weir
warnings.message:
High tides tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible Around high tide 
We are entering a sequence of Spring tides that may lead to flooding. Flooding is possible around 06:45 on Friday 11th September. Flooding is forecast to affect locations at Porlock Bay, with low lying land and roads expected to be most affected, particularly around the coastline between Gore Point and Hurlstone Point including Porlock Weir. The first high tide is at 06:45 on Friday with a peak height of 6.12m and a F4 north westerly wind. The second high tide is at 19:00 on Friday with a peak height of 6.37m and a F4 westerly wind 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded . 
This message will be updated by 12:19PM on 10 September 2026 or as the situation changes.

warnings.label: Tidal River Avon at Bristol, Pill and Shirehampton
warnings.description: Tidal River Avon at Bristol, Pill and Shirehampton
warnings.county: City of Bristol, North Somerset, South Gloucestershire
warnings.message:
High tides this evening may lead to flooding. 

Flooding is possible from 08:00PM to 10:00PM on 12/09. 

Areas most at risk include the tidal River Avon from Sea Mills to Conham in Bristol and between the Avonmouth Bridge and Shirehampton Park including Pill and Shirehampton. The detailed tidal forecast for those who use it is for a peak level at Avonmouth Portbury. The first forecast high water of 7.46 mAODN is at 9:00PM 12/09, which is 0.12 m above tide tables, with Westerly force 5 winds. (mAODN is height above average sea level.) 

We are closely monitoring the situation. 

Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water. 

This message will be updated by 2:00PM on 13/09 or as the situation changes.

warnings.label: The north Norfolk coast from Old Hunstanton, to and including Cley
warnings.description: The north Norfolk coast from Old Hunstanton, to and including Cley
warnings.message:
High tides tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible between 7:15am and 9:15am tomorrow, Sunday 13th September. 
We expect to see water on roads and paths to beaches and on the quays in Brancaster, Burnham Overy, Holkham, Wells and Blakeney. The detailed forecast is for a peak level at Wells of 3.66mAODN at 8:15am, on Saturday 13th September, which is 0.26m above tide tables, wind force 3, westerly. Tides are expected to be higher than usual, due to the forecast weather conditions during spring tides. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded . 
This message will be updated by 3:00PM on 13 September 2026 or as the situation changes.
